deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematical derivations. It is a working memorandum of instrument constants for the Göttingen observatory, plus some administrative numbers.

(1) Mural quadrant (continuing the previous page): the threads (Gänge) of the clamping screws have a pitch of p_K = 0.63 mm. The play (Spielraum) is 13 mm. [My inference: that is about 13/0.63 ≈ 20.6 turns of free travel.]

(2) Beam compass (Stangenzirkel), presumably the one used to measure the quadrant and circle radii on the previous page: the micrometer screw has a pitch of p_M = 0.712 mm per revolution. The index correction (correctio indicis) is +0.05 revolution, i.e. 0.05·0.712 ≈ 0.036 mm.

(3) A correction table for estimated readings. If the fraction of a revolution is estimated rather than read off the divided disc (Scheibe), a correction depends on where an index line stands relative to the drum division. For positions 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 (drum parts, R.) one adds +0.01, +0.31(?), +0.24(?), +0.41(?), +0.19. Several of these are overwritten, so the exact values are uncertain.

In addition, under the mark £, there is a correction for the index line itself at positions 0…10: −0.19(?), −0.02, −0.02, +0.02, +0.04, +0.06, +0.03, +0.06, +0.05, +0.01, +0.02 (several also overwritten). In modern terms this is an empirically tabulated systematic and periodic reading correction of a micrometer drum, interpolated additively: reading_corrected = reading + c1(coarse position) + c2(index line).

(4) Pencil jottings: '19   22(21)', '@ letzte volle W[oche?] 4 / 10'. Meaning uncertain.

(5) 'Witwenkasse' (the Göttingen professors' widows' fund, which Gauss reviewed actuarially in 1845–51). Three census-like rows, one per decade:
- 1823–24: 210 | 13 | 29+4
- 1833–34: 240 | 11 | 34+4
- 1843–44: 250 | 22 | 32+17

The column meanings are not stated. Plausibly they are fund membership or contributors, a yearly count such as deaths or new members, and widows split into two categories. The sums are 33, 38, 49. This is raw data collection, not computation.

(6) Pencil table for 1847–1850 with four day/month entries per year:
- 1847: 19/4, 28/8, 25/10, 26/3
- 1848: 1/5, 9/9, 23/10, 24/3
- 1849: 23/4, 1/9, 22/10, 23/3
- 1850: 22/4, 31/8, 3/10, 22/3

These are not fractions but dates: 19 April, 28 August, 25 October, 26 March, and so on. They fit the beginning and end of the summer semester (April–Aug/Sept) and of the winter semester (October–March) at Göttingen, so they are almost certainly lecture-term dates.
errors: No computational errors can be identified; the page records constants and data rather than derivations.

Several correction values (drum positions 10, 20, 30 and index-line entries 0, 1, 2, 4, 5) are overwritten. The final values are uncertain, and the entry −0.19 for index line 0 is anomalously large compared with its neighbours. It may be a misreading of an overwritten −0.01 or −0.02.

transcription_corrections: The pencil 'fractions' in the 1847–1850 table (19/4, 28/8, …) are day/month dates, not fractions; read e.g. 19 April, 28 August, 25 October, 26 March.
The '+0,01' after 'addirt' is a faint pencil addition.
Correction values at drum positions 10, 20, 30 (+0,31/+0,24/+0,41) are overwritten in ink. The underlying digits differ (e.g. 0,21→0,31?), so the readings are uncertain.
Index-line entries 0, 1, 2, 4, 5 are overwritten. Row 0 may not be −0,19; rows 4/5 may be +0,02→+0,04 and +0,04→+0,06.
'£' is a reference/insertion mark, not a currency sign.
The pencil note 'letzte volle W.' possibly reads 'letzte volle Woche'; the following '4' and '10' stand beneath, apparently forming a 4/10 date-like entry.
